title: Fix the storage-nearly-full repair's dead key lookup so the pre-loss warning can actually fire
why_top: Highest adjusted total (31.9) with no premise dock, and it wins on both metrics that matter: raw/adjusted by 4.2 over frontend-cards-7, and per_round 10.6 versus 9.2. It was active in all three rounds, took two champions, and its two open concerns were both closed on verified ground rather than argued away — C2 by tracing coordinator.readings to its single writer, C3 by showing sensor.py:164 only flips hub_health at >=99 while STORAGE_WARN_PERCENT is 95, so the dead repair is the only warning that arrives before footage is overwritten. I confirmed the core myself: repairs.py:114-115 read `storage_total`/`storage_free`, status.py:237-239 emit only `storage_total_gb`, `storage_free_gb`, and `storage_used_percent`, and a repo-wide grep shows repairs.py is the only reader of the un-suffixed names anywhere. The guard at repairs.py:118 therefore always takes the delete branch and async_create_issue is unreachable. Its rivals all shrank under contest: offline-8 lost its fan-out multiplier outright (docked −6), frontend-cards-7 conceded the disk-integrity half in Round 2 and carries an open concern against the remaining severity claim, and preview-500 struck its own leakage escalation and stopped competing after Round 2.
value_rationale: Like the 85-anchor — a verified defect, a two-line change in one file, trivially reverted — but no test pins it (the harness at tests/test_platforms.py:114-127 only string-matches the source, which is why 1152 tests stayed green) and the symptom is a warning that never appears rather than anything a user can see break, so the evidence of user harm is inferential → 72.
decomposition: In repairs._storage (custom_components/tapo_h500/repairs.py:113-121), read the key status.py actually emits: `used_percent = coordinator.readings.get("storage_used_percent")`, replacing both the storage_total/storage_free lookups and the subtraction.

Keep the unknown-is-not-fine semantics: `if used_percent is None: delete the issue and return` — the old guard at :118 used total and free for exactly this, so it must be rewritten, not just left in place.

Add a real behavioural test to tests/test_platforms.py that calls _storage with a fake coordinator whose readings mirror status.hub_readings' actual key names at 96% and asserts async_create_issue fires, then at 90% asserts it is deleted. This is the missing gate, not a string match.
Run tools/verify.sh and quote the result line.
premise_notes: Premise holds and I re-verified it firsthand: repairs.py:114-115 are the only readers of `storage_total`/`storage_free` in the whole tree, status.py:237-239 emits only the _gb-suffixed pair plus storage_used_percent, so the guard always deletes and the issue is unreachable; the one overstatement flagged (that total/free were only subtraction inputs — they also feed the guard) makes the fix two lines instead of one and changes nothing else.
metrics_note: Trusted raw/adjusted, and it agrees with per_round. Both leading ideas ran all 3 rounds with 2 champions each, so the well-tested lean applies and no per_round normalisation is warranted; correctness-1 leads on raw (31.9 vs 27.7) and on per_round (10.6 vs 9.2) alike. Per_arg is a wash at 5.3 vs 4.6 with champion counts equal, so it added nothing. The one apparent conflict is preview-500's per_round 10.7, a hair above the winner's 10.6, but it sat out a round, its raw is 10.6 lower, and the tie-break on single-round peak favours correctness-1 (8.5 vs 8.0).
strongest_dissent: Tomas Lindqvist's own Round 1 assessment, never fully retired: "the harm is a silent never-firing repair rather than anything a user sees, and it engages no rival." The Round 3 premise check sharpens the residual: sensor.py also ships a storage_full_in forecast sensor alongside storage_used_percent, so the repair is the only push warning, not the only fullness signal — a user who already badges the percent sensor gains nothing from this fix.

minority.why_lost: Lost by 4.2 adjusted points after being docked −2, and it was hollowed out from both sides. Idris Bello's Round 2 challenge verified __init__.py:443-446 re-asks the hub and media.py:57-60 derives paths from slug plus timestamp, so no clip lands mislabeled on disk — the data-integrity half is gone. Then C6 landed against the remaining severity claim and still stands open: _load()'s finally clears _busy and re-renders when the in-flight request returns, so a swallowed click leaves a stale label for seconds, not an empty card until the 60s tick. Mei conceded that in Round 3 and scored 6.3 for it. What survives is a cosmetic mislabel that self-heals, bought with a request-token rewrite of the card's load path — worse impact and worse blast radius than a two-line key fix.
minority.flip_condition: Show a path where the stale response is consumed rather than merely displayed — for example that a user click on a clip row between the swallowed reload and the re-render reads the previous camera's index out of the rendered DOM and hands it to a download or preview call, or that an in-flight _load can fail to reach its finally (an early return or a throw outside the try) and strand the card. Either one restores a real wrong-data outcome and its I8/F9 Round 1 shape, which clears correctness-1's silent-warning ceiling.
